en: The Legend of the Elder Cunda Upāli Chapter 10 [Verse 1] When the Buddha was born in the world, I was a merchant’s son at that time. I went to the Teacher, the Great Sage, and offered him a pair of sandals. [Verse 2] Having made this offering to the Teacher, the Great Sage, I then took refuge in the Buddha, the Dhamma, and the Saṅgha, and undertook the five precepts. [Verse 3] For eighty-four thousand years I practiced the holy life under the dispensation of the Buddha Kassapa. Having performed such merit, I was reborn in the Brahma-world. [Verse 4] From there, passing away, I was reborn in the human world. In my final existence, I was born into a wealthy family. [Verse 5] I was handsome, possessed of great beauty, and endowed with all the marks of excellence. I was skilled in all crafts and possessed of abundant wealth. [Verse 6] I gave alms-food to the Saṅgha of monks headed by the Buddha. Because of that deed, I attained the fruit of stream-entry. [Verse 7] I am now a monk who has reached the end of suffering;

I have attained the goal of the holy life and fulfilled my task. [Verse 8] I have lived the holy life under the dispensation of the Great Sage. I have cast off birth and death; there is no further becoming for me. [Verse 9] This is my last birth; I shall not be born again. I have attained the state of an Arhat, free from all defilements. [Verse 10] I have attained the peaceful, sorrowless state, which is free from fear. I have reached the cool, deathless state, the supreme security from bondage. [Verse 11] I have attained the state of peace, the state of Nibbāna. I have crossed over the flood and am liberated from all bonds. [Verse 12] I have attained the state of peace, the state of Nibbāna. I have reached the far shore of the ocean of suffering and am free from all taints. [Verse 13] I have attained the state of peace, the state of Nibbāna. I have reached the island of safety and am liberated from all suffering. [Verse 14] I have attained the state of peace, the state of Nibbāna. I have reached the city of Nirvana and am liberated from all bonds. [Verse 15] I have attained the state of peace, the state of Nibbāna. I have reached the state of bliss and am liberated from all defilements. [Verse 16] I have attained the state of peace, the state of Nibbāna. I have reached the state of purity and am liberated from all fetters. [Verse 17] I have attained the state of peace, the state of Nibbāna. I have reached the state of liberation and am liberated from all attachments. [Verse 18] I have attained the state of peace, the state of Nibbāna. I have reached the state of the Tathāgata and am liberated from all stains. [Verse 19] I have attained the state of peace, the state of Nibbāna. I have reached the state of the Arahant and am liberated from all craving. [Verse 20] I have attained the state of peace, the state of Nibbāna. I have reached the state of the Victor and am liberated from all conceit. [Verse 21] I have attained the state of peace, the state of Nibbāna. I have reached the state of the Conqueror and am liberated from all delusion. [Verse 22] I have attained the state of peace, the state of Nibbāna. I have reached the state of the Buddha and am liberated from all ignorance. [Verse 23] I have attained the state of peace, the state of Nibbāna. I have reached the state of the Fully Enlightened One and am liberated from all doubt. [Verse 24] I have attained the state of peace, the state of Nibbāna. I have reached the state of the All-Knowing One and am liberated from all hindrances. [Verse 25] I have attained the state of peace, the state of Nibbāna. I have reached the state of the Omniscient One and am liberated from all obscurations. [Verse 26] I have attained the state of peace, the state of Nibbāna. I have reached the state of the All-Seeing One and am liberated from all darkness. [Verse 27] I have attained the state of peace, the state of Nibbāna. I have reached the state of the Light-Maker and am liberated from all gloom. [Verse 28] I have attained the state of peace, the state of Nibbāna. I have reached the state of the Radiant One and am liberated from all shadows. [Verse 29] I have attained the state of peace, the state of Nibbāna. I have reached the state of the Glorious One and am liberated from all obscurity. [Verse 30] I have attained the state of peace, the state of Nibbāna. I have reached the state of the Splendid One and am liberated from all dullness. [Verse 31] I have attained the state of peace, the state of Nibbāna. I have reached the state of the Majestic One and am liberated from all weakness. [Verse 32] I have attained the state of peace, the state of Nibbāna. I have reached the state of the Sublime One and am liberated from all frailty. [Verse 33] I have attained the state of peace, the state of Nibbāna. I have reached the state of the Exalted One and am liberated from all instability. [Verse 34] I have attained the state of peace, the state of Nibbāna. I have reached the state of the Noble One and am liberated from all wavering. [Verse 35] I have attained the state of peace, the state of Nibbāna. I have reached the state of the Supreme One and am liberated from all agitation. [Verse 36] I have attained the state of peace, the state of Nibbāna. I have reached the state of the Peerless One and am liberated from all turbulence. [Verse 37] I have attained the state of peace, the state of Nibbāna. I have reached the state of the Unsurpassed One and am liberated from all unrest. [Verse 38] I have attained the state of peace, the state of Nibbāna. I have reached the state of the Incomparable One and am liberated from all conflict. [Verse 39] I have attained the state of peace, the state of Nibbāna. I have reached the state of the Matchless One and am liberated from all strife. [Verse 40] I have attained the state of peace, the state of Nibbāna. I have reached the state of the Unequaled One and am liberated from all discord.

[Verse 41] I have attained the state of peace, the state of Nibbāna. I have reached the state of the Unrivaled One and am liberated from all contention. [Verse 42] I have attained the state of peace, the state of Nibbāna. I have reached the state of the Unconquered One and am liberated from all defeat. [Verse 43] I have attained the state of peace, the state of Nibbāna. I have reached the state of the Invincible One and am liberated from all subjugation. [Verse 44] I have attained the state of peace, the state of Nibbāna. I have reached the state of the Unassailable One and am liberated from all assault. [Verse 45] I have attained the state of peace, the state of Nibbāna. I have reached the state of the Unshakeable One and am liberated from all trembling. [Verse 46] I have attained the state of peace, the state of Nibbāna. I have reached the state of the Steadfast One and am liberated from all wavering. [Verse 47] I have attained the state of peace, the state of Nibbāna. I have reached the state of the Firm One and am liberated from all fluctuation. [Verse 48] I have attained the state of peace, the state of Nibbāna.
“Having had a sacred offering made for the Blessed One Siddhattha, the World-Chief, the Neutral One;”
I covered [the stupa] with jasmine flowers.
Having finished that floral work,
I offered it to the Buddha.
Having taken the remaining flowers,
I offered them to the Buddha,
who resembled a priceless golden ornament.
To the Buddha, the leader supreme in the world,
with a clear heart and joyful mind,
I offered a garland of flowers.
The Perfectly Awakened One, whose doubts have been dispelled and who is honored by those who have crossed the floods,
sat down amidst the community of monks.
He spoke these verses:
“To him who gave me this flower-vessel, wafting a divine fragrance...”
I shall proclaim this;
listen as I speak.
Having passed away from here, this person—
Honored by the assembly of gods,
and strewn with jasmine flowers,
he will go to the world of the gods.
His celestial mansion,
made of gold and fashioned of jewels,
shall appear lofty in the sky.
Developed through the power of meritorious deeds,
he will exercise divine sovereignty seventy-four times.
He will experience prosperity,
honored by celestial nymphs;
he will rule over three hundred kingdoms on earth.
He shall dwell upon the earth;
and seventy-five times he shall become a wheel-turning monarch.
He will become a lord of men named Dujjaya;
having experienced that merit, he shall attain his goal.
Supported by his own wholesome deeds,
he will not go to a state of ruin, but will return to the human realm.
His accumulated gold amounts to no less than one hundred koṭis;
he will be reborn in a womb.
He will be a brahmin;
the wise son of Vaṅganta,
the beloved legitimate offspring of Sārī.
And having gone forth later on in the teaching of Aṅgīrasa,
he was known by the name Cūḷacunda.
He will become a disciple of the Teacher.
While still a novice, being virtuous,
he will be one whose taints are destroyed.
“Having fully understood all taints,
he will attain Nibbāna, free from taints.
Thus I attended upon the Great Hero.
And many other virtuous ones;
I attended upon my brother for the sake of attaining the supreme goal.
Having attended upon my brother,
I placed the relic in a bowl and offered it to the Fully Enlightened One.
The eldest in the world, the bull among men—
the Buddha, in this world with its devas, having grasped him with both hands—
Displaying that relic,
he praised his chief disciple:
"My mind is well-liberated."
My faith is firmly established;
having fully understood all taints,
I dwell free from taints.
The analytical knowledges have been attained, the liberations have been touched,
and the six direct knowledges have been realized.
“Such is the teaching of the Buddha.
Thus indeed did the venerable elder Cunda speak these verses.
This is the tenth *apadāna* of the elder Cunda.
The fifth chapter, the Upāli-vagga.
Its summary verse:
Upāli, Soṇa, Bhaddiya.
The elephants that carry out the decision;
the covering, the bed, and the walkway;
Subhadda and the one called Cunda.
One hundred and forty-six verses,
and four more than that.
